claims.statement: An expired ignore entry never excuses a changed file; it is reported as expired and the file stays uncovered.

claims.statement: A changed test file is covered only when it resolves as a defender of some claim; a test that defends nothing is uncovered.

faults.description: Any test file counts as covered, whether or not a claim names it.

claims.statement: When a reference is known and the change touches unclaimed source files, status reports unclaimed-changes before any evidence state, with the file as the next action.

faults.description: Unclaimed changes never become the state; evidence states hide them.

claims.statement: The brief renders unclaimed changes before the ranked findings, so an agent writes the claim before more code.

faults.description: The unclaimed block is never rendered in the TEXT brief (the markdown renderer has its own claim).

claims.statement: The release version check exits non-zero when any version surface is out of step with package.json; a release can never ship with drifting version strings.

claims.statement: scaffold proposes field-dropped only for a line that can be removed on its own: balanced brackets, and comma-terminated or followed by the closer. A multi-line property is never proposed.

faults.description: The completeness check is defeated; a property whose value continues on the next line is proposed and the fault would not compile.

claims.statement: scaffold proposes argument-swapped only when the argument is derived from a parameter of the enclosing function or a request-like value; a call with a literal or unrelated argument is never proposed.

faults.description: Every first argument counts as derived.

claims.statement: admit says ADMITTED only when every probed fault of the claim is killed; a single surviving, uncovered, unverifiable, invalid, timed-out or flaky fault blocks admission.

faults.description: One killed fault is enough to admit; a test that kills F2 but lets F1 survive is admitted.

claims.statement: When a commit is probed as committed although defender/target files are dirty (explicit --ref or --ignore-dirty), the evidence records those files under repo.ignoredDirty.

faults.description: The ignored files are warned about but never recorded; the evidence looks like a clean probe.

claims.statement: A test file that mocks the target module is never counted as a defender of a claim about that module; it is listed as mocking instead.

faults.description: Mocking files are treated like any other importer and counted as defenders.

claims.statement: A test file that mocks the target and never asserts on anything imported from it carries the mocked-never-asserted signal (or the annotated form when the author gave a reason).

faults.description: The signal is never produced; an unasserted mock looks like any other mock.

claims.statement: Path aliases declared in a tsconfig reached through `references` (the Vite layout) and in a vite/vitest `resolve.alias` are resolved when discovering defenders.

faults.description: Referenced tsconfigs are ignored; only the root tsconfig's paths count.

claims.statement: File walking never descends into node_modules, .git, dist, coverage or .testguard; test discovery and defender globs cannot pick up a dependency's or a build's test files.

claims.statement: baseline --restamp moves head only when a clean probe reproduced exactly the baseline's fingerprints; a frozen contract is never silently rewritten.

claims.statement: A baseline frozen from working-tree-snapshot evidence records the snapshot commit, so a reader can tell its head is the parent of the commit that carries the tests.

faults.description: The snapshot is dropped; the baseline looks like a clean freeze of its parent commit.

claims.statement: Ancestry between a baseline's head and HEAD is decided by git (merge-base --is-ancestor); a commit that is not in HEAD's history is never reported as an ancestor.

claims.statement: Every session-start hook command the README shows is one the code actually emits; documentation that describes a hook the tool no longer writes is a finding, not a detail.

claims.statement: A probe's reported cost is every run it paid for — the clean baseline runs and any escalation runs, not only the runs made with the fault applied. A cost report that undercounts the baseline understates the gate by more than half.

faults.description: Only the fault runs are counted, so the clean baseline runs — half the wall clock — vanish from the report.

claims.statement: A defender file is called shared only when more than one distinct CLAIM names it. One claim probing several faults through the same file is not sharing, and reporting it as such would point the reader at a split that saves nothing.

faults.description: Sharing is counted by runs rather than by distinct claims, so a single claim with two faults is reported as a shared defender.

claims.statement: A probe reports progress whether or not stderr is a terminal. The rewriting line is a rendering choice for a human; CI, a redirected log and an agent harness get append-only lines. Twenty silent minutes is indistinguishable from a hang.

faults.description: Progress is silent again whenever stderr is not a terminal, which is every automated context.

claims.statement: Progress is written to stderr, never stdout. stdout carries the result — with --json it is one document and nothing else — so a progress line there does not degrade the output, it destroys it for every consumer that parses it.

faults.description: Progress is written to stdout, so any consumer piping --json into a parser gets progress lines mixed into the document.
